name: String Table Editor
blurb: multilingual strings in a table, out as resource files
intro: Paste a spreadsheet of strings (key, one column per language, optional comment) as CSV or TSV. It writes one resource file per language for Android, iOS, JSON or Flutter ARB with the platform's escaping, and checks for missing translations, duplicate keys, invalid key names and placeholders that differ from the base language.

inputs.label: String table (CSV or TSV, header row first)
inputs.default:
key,en,tr,de,comment
app_name,Redline,Redline,Redline,Launcher label
welcome_title,"Welcome, %1$s!","Hoş geldin, %1$s!","Willkommen, %1$s!",Home screen header
items_left,%1$d items left,%1$d öğe kaldı,,Cart badge
save,Save,Kaydet,Speichern,
error_network,"Can't reach the server.
Check your connection.",Sunucuya ulaşılamıyor.,"Server nicht erreichbar.",Shown in a dialog
inputs.help: Header: key, then language codes (en, tr, pt-BR), optionally a comment column. Copy straight from a spreadsheet (tab-separated) or paste CSV; quote values that contain the separator or a line break.

inputs.label: Base language
inputs.help: The source language column; placeholders are checked against it. Empty = the first language column.

examples.title: Web strings from a spreadsheet as nested JSON, with a placeholder mistake

input.table:
key	en	fr	pt-BR
login.title	Sign in	Connexion	Entrar
login.button	Continue	Continuer	Continuar
login.greeting	Hi {name}	Salut {nom}	Olá {name}
cart.total	Total: %s	Total : %s

usage: Give table as CSV or TSV text (header: key, language codes, optional comment column), format = android | ios | json | arb, base = the source language code, missing = omit | base | empty, and nestKeys (JSON only). It returns one text output per language holding the finished resource file (named like values-tr/strings.xml), a coverage table per language, a Problems table (duplicate keys, invalid names, placeholder mismatches, non-positional Android placeholders) and the list of untranslated keys. Use it to turn a translators' sheet into app resources or to audit a sheet before release.
sources: Android Developers, String resources: formatting and styling (escaping of apostrophes, quotes, @ and ?, positional format arguments)
Apple, String Resources Programming Guide / Localizable.strings file format
